# manim-marimo 0.0.1

manim-marimo renders [ManimGL](https://github.com/3b1b/manim) scenes from the
results of a [marimo](https://marimo.io/) notebook, as
[marimo-studio](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/) views. The
notebook computes the values. A scene in the view animates them, and Studio
renders the movie again whenever a value changes.

## Install

Declare `manim-marimo[render]` in the notebook's script metadata, with the
pixi tables that install ManimGL's OpenGL and Pango libraries, and open the
notebook in a pixi sandbox:

```sh
uvx --with manim-marimo marimo edit analysis.py --sandbox=pixi --watch
```

Click **Add view** and choose **Manim animation**.
[Getting started](https://peter-gy.github.io/manim-marimo/guide/getting-started)
shows the complete metadata.

## Read notebook results in a scene

- `value()`, `output()`, and `cell()` read a notebook value, a cell's output
  as an image, or a whole cell. Studio finds the reads in the scene's source
  without running it, and renders the scene again when one of them changes.
- `output("chart", height=2.6)` draws a matplotlib figure or a Vega-Lite chart
  at the height the scene gives it, so its labels keep their point size.
- Each read takes a `default`, so the view builds and previews before a kernel
  connects.

## Render and publish movies

- Scenes render in the `manim-marimo-worker` command from the notebook's pixi
  environment, under Studio's deadlines and cancellation. A render publishes
  `animation.mp4`, its poster, and its metadata together.
- `view.toml` sets `quality` to `draft`, `preview`, or `production`.
- On Linux, scenes render through Mesa's EGL driver, so servers and CI runners
  render without a display or a GPU.
- `zero-python` exports render every scene once per state that `states.yaml`
  lists, and the static site plays them without Python.

## Trace shapes to the notebook

Each render traces the shapes in its frames to the notebook results they show,
such as `joint[2][3]` for one cell of a probability table. With
[Lens](https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo-lens), Studio's preview makes each
shape a target that follows it as the movie plays and selects the cell that
computed it.

## Create views from Studio and from agents

- The `manim-marimo/manim:default` starter creates a scene, a page with a
  video player, and the notebook's output cells. Studio's New view dialog
  shows it with a preview and writes the view's title into the page.
- The wheel ships an agent skill.
  `uvx --with manim-marimo agent-plugins read manim-marimo` prints it for
  Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents.

## Examples

[Four example notebooks](https://peter-gy.github.io/manim-marimo/examples/)
animate a notebook's dataflow graph, Fourier drawings, the convolution of two
dice, and an epidemic simulation.

## Compatibility

manim-marimo 0.0.1 supports Python 3.10 through 3.14, marimo-studio 0.4, and
ManimGL 1.7.2 or newer within 1.7. Studio and the worker must run the same
manim-marimo release.
